groups.text: It is currently 17 degrees and cloudy in Berlin-Tempelhof.
With the morning weather set, here is the news.

Donald Trump is claiming that the governments of Hugo Chávez and Nicolás Maduro plotted to electronically manipulate election results between 2004 and 2020. He based these assertions on declassified CIA documents during a speech on July 16, but those reports actually contradict his claims. The CIA findings state there is no definitive evidence of large-scale electronic fraud and conclude that neither the Venezuelan government nor Smartmatic could alter elections outside of Venezuela. While Trump uses this to suggest vulnerability in U.S. systems, analysts note that Chavismo typically relies on political disqualifications rather than electronic hacking to gain advantages at home. Some observers view these claims as a desperate attempt by Trump to change electoral rules or demotivate Democratic and independent voters ahead of the November midterm elections, where analysts predict a failure for the Republican Party.

The General Staff of the Armed Forces of Ukraine reports that Russia has lost around 1,428,930 troops since the full-scale invasion began on February 24, 2022. This total includes 1,520 casualties suffered over the past day alone. Equipment losses are also steep, with figures including 12,156 tanks, 46,261 artillery systems, and 416,656 drones. While Ukraine keeps its own losses secret, a January 2026 report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies estimated Ukrainian casualties between 500,000 and 600,000 through December 2025. Meanwhile, in Hungary, President Tamas Sulyok has agreed to step down on July 20 after signing constitutional changes that end his term. This follows a push from Prime Minister Peter Magyar, who won the April elections and replaced Viktor Orban. Sulyok criticized the move as a violation of constitutional values, while Magyar accused him of covering up abuses by the previous regime.

Tensions are escalating between the United States and Iran as both sides signal they no longer feel bound by their framework agreement. Following a lethal Iranian attack in Jordan that killed two American soldiers and left another missing, the U.S. military launched a series of bombardments on Sunday night. CENTCOM reports these strikes successfully targeted Iranian air defense and coastal surveillance facilities to punish the Revolutionary Guard. The U.S. also aims to weaken Iran's ability to threaten commercial shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. In response, Iran launched attacks against two U.S. bases in Kuwait, while rockets struck areas near Gheshm Island in the Persian Gulf. This marks a sharp spike in violence; it is the first time in nearly five months that the U.S. has reported fatalities from Iranian fire, bringing the official death toll of American soldiers in this conflict to sixteen.

Ukrainian viewers are shifting their habits on YouTube, creating a new financial incentive for content creators. According to an analysis by Detector Media and Olga Tyshchuk of the Tyshchuk Digital Hub, there is a clear link between language and profitability. Channels that feature a higher share of Ukrainian-language content now show better prospects for revenue growth compared to those that do not. This shift suggests that as more people choose to watch series in Ukrainian, the economic rewards are following the audience's linguistic preferences. While general viewing dynamics for serial content continue to evolve, the financial advantage is currently tilting toward native language production. For media producers and digital hubs, this means that investing in Ukrainian-language scripts and dubbing is no longer just a cultural choice, but a strategic move to increase overall income on the platform.

The Pakistan Paediatric Association is urging the Drug Regulatory Authority of Pakistan to exempt ten-cc conventional syringes from a looming ban to protect neonatal and paediatric care. This request follows a surge in HIV cases linked to unsafe medical practices and the reuse of contaminated syringes. In response to that crisis, the regulator has imposed a complete ban on non-insulin one-cc disposable syringes starting December 31, 2026, with a further ban on the retail sale of ten-cc disposal syringes beginning January 1, 2027. Dr. Muhammad Khalid Shafi of the association warns that while eliminating syringe reuse is a commendable goal, this blanket policy creates severe unintended risks for the youngest patients. He argues that public health measures must remain evidence-based and aligned with clinical realities to curb transmission without compromising patient outcomes during this national emergency.

The U.S. military has launched its eighth consecutive night of strikes against Iran to punish the Revolutionary Guard for an attack in Jordan that killed two American service members and left a third missing. Tehran responded by launching explosive drones at two U.S. bases in Kuwait, prompting the Kuwaiti military to engage hostile missiles and drones targeting local oil facilities and a power plant. In a separate security move in Israel, Environment Minister Idit Silman has reclassified Nile crocodiles as cultivated wild animals rather than wild animals. This change allows approved security organizations, such as the Israel Prison Service, to keep the reptiles for security purposes subject to government approval. Far-right Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir reportedly intends to use the crocodiles to prevent escapes at Ketziot prison, which primarily holds Palestinian security prisoners.

Tension is mounting in New York as fans gather for the World Cup final between Spain and Argentina. Argentinian supporters have already taken over Times Square just hours before kick-off. On the streets, the debate centers on which star player holds the edge: Lamine Yamal or Lionel Messi. This clash of talent follows a tournament where Spanish supporters recently celebrated a victory over France in Dallas. While fans argue over their favorite players, journalists from France 24 have spent several weeks on the ground to cover the event. Their teams are operating from press boxes and mixed zones to capture the final moments of the competition before the last whistle blows.
After the headlines, back to the weather.
This afternoon will be cloudy with rain chances up to 80 percent and temperatures between 16 and 21 degrees.
And from the weather, a quick look at the calendar.
On your calendar today: Your personal calendar has an all-day event for the twenty-twenty-six summer holidays in Berlin.
And that's it for your personal morning broadcast.
[mature adult voice, intensely emotional, tender, radiant; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
[very very long pause before speaking; then mature adult voice, most emotional, strong, warm, radiant, deeply encouraging; hold a long breath after Rise] Rise... and shine.
